GRU4Rec’s strongest direct precedent is BPR-max: softmax-weight negative scores, then minimize −log Σⱼ[wⱼσ(s₊−sⱼ)], with the paper’s weighted negative-score regularization. This concentrates gradients on competitive negatives, addressing dilution from averaging many easy BPR pairs. The official implementation recommends BPR-max or cross-entropy over ordinary BPR/TOP1. These findings originate in session recommendation; gains on the four Amazon categories remain unverified. [Original paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [official implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec).

Recent evidence cautions against assuming harder or popularity-weighted negatives always improve accuracy. A 2024 sequential-recommendation comparison found sampling effects depend on dataset popularity distributions; uniform sampling favored head items, while popularity-based sampling offered more balanced performance at some overall accuracy cost. Another 2024 study improved sampled WARP/LambdaRank through corrected rank estimates, highlighting sampling bias. False negatives remain a concern: UFNRec explicitly models them, although its teacher-based recipe is outside this experiment’s intended single-model objective change. [Sampling comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276), [rank correction](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/), [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116).

Suggested experiment, inferred from these findings: keep the corrected GRU backbone fixed; compare baseline loss against regularized BPR-max and multi-negative sampled cross-entropy using identical negative pools. Exclude padding, the target and known training positives; deduplicate candidates. Retain random negatives alongside moderate hardness weighting rather than selecting only the highest-scoring items. These safeguards reduce known collisions without identifying every latent false negative. Select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, retaining one checkpoint per category.
